module_intro: Deepens Power of 3: the three phases (Accumulation, Manipulation, Distribution), Daily PO3 (classic mapping, opening-price relationship, visual signature), Session PO3 (fractal), Weekly PO3, manipulation relative to liquidity, PO3 + HTF bias, and PO3 failure/alternative daily delivery.
prerequisites_stated_in_text: Requires Beginner Module 9 (Power of 3) and Intermediate Modules 1-9.
module_objectives: Define Accumulation, Manipulation and Distribution within the ICT Power of 3 (PO3 / AMD) framework.
Map the three phases onto the daily candle and onto the Asian -> London -> New York session sequence.
Recognise PO3 structure on the weekly timeframe.
Relate the daily opening price to the location of manipulation.
Integrate PO3 with higher-timeframe bias and the Draw on Liquidity.
Identify PO3 failure and alternative daily delivery profiles.
Use PO3 as a contextual map rather than as a standalone entry signal.

raw_sections.Accumulation: Accumulation is the relatively quiet, range-bound phase in which positions are built. Volatility is typically lower; a clear high and low of the accumulation range form. On the daily profile this often corresponds to the Asian session. Liquidity builds above the range high and below the range low.
raw_sections.Manipulation: Manipulation is the false or engineered move outside the accumulation range. Its purpose is to run stops, attract breakout traders, and generate the liquidity required for the subsequent true move. On the daily profile this frequently appears as the London Open sweep of the Asian range (Judas Swing). The manipulation leaves a wick on the higher-timeframe candle.
raw_sections.Distribution: Distribution is the real directional expansion. Price reverses through the accumulation range and delivers toward the intended liquidity objective. On the daily profile this often occurs during the New York session (or the latter part of London into New York). The body of the daily candle is largely the product of the distribution phase.

raw_sections.Classic Mapping:
A common daily mapping is:

832. Accumulation - Asian session range.

833. Manipulation - London Open sweep of one side of the Asian range.

834. Distribution - London continuation or New York expansion toward the opposing liquidity / HTF target.
raw_sections.Opening Price Relationship: The daily opening price is a useful reference. On many bullish PO3 days the manipulation occurs below the open (sell-side raid) and distribution carries price above the open toward buy-side objectives. On many bearish PO3 days the manipulation occurs above the open and distribution carries price lower. The open is not a magic level, but its relationship to the manipulation wick is a frequent visual signature of the completed daily candle.
raw_sections.Visual Signature of a Classic Bullish Da: The finished daily candle often shows: a lower wick (manipulation of sell-side liquidity), an open somewhere in the middle or lower half, and a close near the high (distribution). The mirror image appears on classic bearish days.

concepts.name: Session Power of 3
concepts.why_it_matters: When the daily PO3 is clear, the session PO3 is used to time the entry: wait for the session-level manipulation (local liquidity sweep) and the subsequent displacement that begins distribution, then enter on the retracement into the PD array created by that displacement.

raw_sections.Fractal Nature: The same three phases can appear inside a single kill zone or session. A New York Open window may itself accumulate briefly, manipulate a local high or low, then distribute. Recognising the phase inside the session prevents the trader from entering during manipulation and calling it distribution.
raw_sections.Practical Use: When the daily PO3 is clear, the session PO3 is used to time the entry: wait for the session-level manipulation (local liquidity sweep) and the subsequent displacement that begins distribution, then enter on the retracement into the PD array created by that displacement.

raw_sections.Typical Mapping:
On the weekly candle a frequent (though not rigid) profile is:

835. Accumulation - early week (often Monday) range-building.

836. Manipulation - mid-week sweep of the early-week high or low.

837. Distribution - later-week expansion toward the weekly Draw on Liquidity.
raw_sections.Intermediate Application: Weekly PO3 supplies a higher-timeframe context for the daily narrative. A trader who sees the week still in accumulation will treat early-week directional signals with more caution than a trader who sees clear weekly distribution underway.

raw_sections.Purpose of Manipulation: Manipulation is not random noise. It is directed at the liquidity that has accumulated above or below the accumulation range (and often at the Asian range extremes). The side that is manipulated frequently reveals the side that was needed for the subsequent distribution.
raw_sections.Link to Module 2 and Module 9: The liquidity hierarchy and the Asian range references studied earlier are exactly the pools that the manipulation phase is designed to raid. Recognising which pool was taken is the first clue to the likely direction of distribution.

raw_sections.Alignment: The highest-quality daily PO3 profiles are those that align with the higher-timeframe bias and Draw on Liquidity. A bullish daily PO3 that occurs while the weekly and daily narratives are also bullish, and while price is in discount relative to the relevant dealing range, is a high-confluence context.
raw_sections.Conflict: A daily PO3 profile that points opposite to the higher-timeframe bias is lower probability or may represent only a corrective day inside a larger opposing narrative. Intermediate discipline is to favour the higher-timeframe story when the two conflict.

concepts.name: PO3 Failure and Alternative Daily Delivery

raw_sections.PO3 Failure:
PO3 fails when the expected distribution does not materialise, or when the manipulation is itself continued rather than reversed. Examples:

838. Price sweeps the Asian range and keeps going (continuation through the manipulated side rather than reversal).

839. Both sides of the Asian range are swept and the day closes as a doji or inside day with no clear distribution.

840. Distribution begins but is reversed by a higher-timeframe opposing force before the daily target is reached.
raw_sections.Alternative Profiles: Not every day prints a textbook PO3. Alternative profiles include trend days with little manipulation, range days with multiple small AMD cycles, and news-driven expansions that ignore the usual session sequence. The intermediate student recognises these alternatives rather than forcing every day into the three-phase template.
raw_sections.Response to Failure: When the expected PO3 fails, the trader does not insist on the original idea. The higher-timeframe narrative is re-checked, the day's Draw on Liquidity is reassessed, and if necessary the trader stands aside.

rules.statement: Classic daily PO3 mapping: Accumulation = Asian session range; Manipulation = London Open sweep of one side of the Asian range; Distribution = London continuation or New York expansion toward the opposing liquidity/HTF target. Visual signature of a classic bullish daily PO3: a lower wick (manipulation of sell-side liquidity), an open somewhere in the middle or lower half, and a close near the high (distribution); mirror image on classic bearish days.

Typical weekly PO3 mapping (not rigid): Accumulation = early week (often Monday) range-building; Manipulation = mid-week sweep of the early-week high or low; Distribution = later-week expansion toward the weekly Draw on Liquidity. A trader who sees the week still in accumulation should treat early-week directional signals with more caution than one who sees clear weekly distribution underway.
rules.exceptions_or_qualifiers: Described as a frequent, not rigid, profile.

rules.statement: Session PO3 is fractal: the same three phases can appear inside a single kill zone or session (e.g. a New York Open window may itself accumulate briefly, manipulate a local high or low, then distribute). When the daily PO3 is clear, the session PO3 is used to time entry: wait for session-level manipulation (local liquidity sweep) and subsequent displacement beginning distribution, then enter on the retracement into the PD array created by that displacement.

The highest-quality daily PO3 profiles align with the higher-timeframe bias and Draw on Liquidity (e.g. a bullish daily PO3 while weekly and daily narratives are also bullish and price is in discount). A daily PO3 profile pointing opposite to the HTF bias is lower probability or may represent only a corrective day inside a larger opposing narrative; intermediate discipline favours the HTF story when the two conflict.

PO3 failure examples: (1) price sweeps the Asian range and keeps going (continuation through the manipulated side rather than reversal); (2) both sides of the Asian range are swept and the day closes as a doji/inside day with no clear distribution; (3) distribution begins but is reversed by a higher-timeframe opposing force before the daily target is reached. Alternative profiles (not textbook PO3) include trend days with little manipulation, range days with multiple small AMD cycles, and news-driven expansions ignoring the usual session sequence. When the expected PO3 fails, the trader does not insist on the original idea -- the HTF narrative is re-checked, the day's Draw on Liquidity is reassessed, and if necessary the trader stands aside.

examples.content:
HTF: Weekly and daily bias bullish; price in discount; Draw on Liquidity is buy-side above a prior daily high.

Accumulation: Asian session prints a tight range, high 1.0850 / low 1.0810.

Manipulation: London Open sweeps the Asian low to 1.0795, triggering sell-side stops and attracting breakdown sellers.

Distribution: Price displaces higher, breaks short-term structure, leaves a bullish FVG / Order Block, and expands through the Asian high. New York continues the expansion toward the daily buy-side objective.

Daily candle result: lower wick (manipulation), open in the lower half, close near the high (distribution). Entry was available on the retracement into the London-created PD array during the distribution phase.

This profile is aligned with the HTF narrative and is therefore high quality.
examples.interpretation_given_in_text: Demonstrates a classic bullish daily PO3 mapped onto Asian/London/New York sessions.

relationships.statement: Sessions (Module 9) supply the time windows. PO3 supplies the phase labels for those windows: Asian often accumulates, London often manipulates, New York often distributes. Liquidity (Module 2) is what manipulation seeks. Displacement and MSS (Module 3) confirm the transition from manipulation to distribution. PD arrays and OTE (Modules 4 - 7) refine the entry during the distribution-phase retracement. The multi-timeframe narrative (Module 8) decides whether the daily PO3 is aligned with the larger story. Failure recognition prevents forcing the template onto every day.

no_trade_conditions.statement: When the expected PO3 fails or a day prints as a non-textbook alternative profile with no clear narrative, the trader does not insist on the original idea and should stand aside if necessary after reassessing the HTF narrative and Draw on Liquidity.

key_terms: Power of 3 (PO3) / AMD - Accumulation, Manipulation, Distribution sequence.
Accumulation - quiet range-building phase in which positions are established.
Manipulation - engineered move outside the accumulation range to raid liquidity.
Distribution - true directional expansion toward the intended objective.
Daily PO3 - the three phases mapped onto the daily candle and its sessions.
Session PO3 - the same three phases appearing inside a single session or kill zone.
Weekly PO3 - the three phases mapped onto the weekly candle.
PO3 failure - expected distribution does not occur, or manipulation continues instead of reversing.
Alternative daily delivery - trend days, range days, or news-driven profiles that do not follow classic PO3.
module_review_notes.beginner_summary: Beginner teaching introduced Power of 3 as the idea that price accumulates, manipulates and then distributes. Intermediate teaching maps those phases onto concrete sessions, links them to the opening price and to liquidity, requires alignment with the higher-timeframe narrative, and explicitly trains recognition of failure and alternative profiles.
module_review_notes.concept_relationships_summary: PO3 is the phase template that sits on top of the session structure (Module 9). It explains why the Asian range is marked, why London often sweeps it, and why New York often continues. All prior tools (liquidity, displacement, PD arrays, OTE, multi-timeframe narrative) are applied inside the phase that is currently active.
module_review_notes.practical_chart_exercise:
For the next five trading days:

- Before London, mark the Asian range and state the expected PO3 direction given the HTF bias.

- During London, record whether manipulation of the Asian range occurred and on which side.

- During New York, record whether distribution in the expected direction materialised.

- At the close, sketch the daily candle and label Accumulation, Manipulation and Distribution (or note that the day was an alternative profile).

- Write one sentence on whether the day's PO3 was aligned with the HTF narrative and one lesson for the next day.
self_test_questions: Define Accumulation, Manipulation and Distribution in one sentence each.
How does a classic bullish daily PO3 typically map onto the Asian, London and New York sessions?
What is the usual relationship between the daily open and the manipulation wick on a bullish PO3 day?
When should a daily PO3 profile be treated as lower quality?
Give two examples of PO3 failure or alternative daily delivery.
Why is PO3 described as a map rather than as a signal?
common_misconceptions: "Every day is a textbook PO3." - False. Alternative profiles are common; forcing the template creates errors.
"Manipulation always reverses." - False. Sometimes the sweep is the start of true continuation.
"If I see accumulation I should enter." - False. Entry belongs in the distribution phase after confirmation.
"Weekly PO3 is too slow to matter." - False. It supplies the higher-timeframe context that grades the daily profile.
"PO3 replaces the need for displacement and MSS." - False. Those remain the confirmation tools inside the distribution phase.
